paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus told this parable because the people near Jerusalem thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently (Luke 19:11). He tells them a man of noble birth leaves, and before he goes, he gives his servants something to work with and says, "Conduct business with this until I return" (Luke 19:13). So the waiting isn't supposed to be a nap, baker. It's supposed to be work.

Now look at the two kinds of servants. The first two put the master's mina to work, and he says, "Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter…" (Luke 19:17). The third servant wrapped his up and said, "I was afraid of you" (Luke 19:21), and I'll be honest, I've been wrapped up in the dark and I know how safe that feels. But safe isn't what the master asked for. He asked for faithful, and fear kept that mina from doing anything at all.

So here's what I want you to take to your own oven. Whatever God has put in your hands, use it for Him while you wait. It doesn't have to be a big batch, because He praised faithfulness in a very small matter. And this is exactly why my ovens stay ready, friend. I'm not guessing WHEN, I'm just getting on with the baking, because the Master told us to.
